claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has previously been produced in a hierarchical-heterostructured state with multilevel chemical fluctuations.

A hybrid micro-mechanical-testing and multi-fidelity machine-learning approach can accurately predict bulk Young’s modulus, yield strength, and fracture toughness for hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
The proposed approach integrates nanoindentation, micro-tensile testing, and micro-notch testing with machine learning.
Nanoindentation supplies local-stiffness information relevant to Young’s modulus.
Micro-tensile tests supply local-yield information relevant to bulk yield strength.
Micro-notch tests supply crack-initiation information relevant to bulk fracture toughness.
The machine-learning model will be calibrated with a limited dataset from CALPHAD, first-principles, and thermophysical calculations.
Localized phase compositions and the distribution of chemical fluctuations can serve as microstructural fingerprints connecting microscale responses to bulk mechanical properties.
Microscale measurements capture local deformation modes and crack-initiation events.
Statistically integrating microscale measurements with physics-based descriptors provides a proxy for interactions governing macroscopic mechanical behavior.
Using experimental microscale data in the model reduces reliance on computationally intensive full-scale simulations.
The hybrid method is expected to improve prediction accuracy by approximately 30–50% relative to conventional simulation-only workflows.
The hybrid method is expected to reduce computational time by up to 80% relative to conventional simulation-only workflows.
Existing baseline approaches rely on thermophysical calculations, CALPHAD, first-principles methods, and machine learning without integrated microscale experimental input.
The approach may become unreliable when microscale tests are unrepresentative of macroscale behavior because of extreme heterogeneity.
The approach may become unreliable when deformation mechanisms arise outside those represented in the training data.
The approach may become unreliable at high strain rates or extreme temperatures outside the model’s training domain.
A blinded prospective comparison will use independent full-scale tensile and fracture measurements as reference outcomes for the model predictions.
The hypothesis is falsified if more than 20% of samples have greater than 10% prediction error in the measured bulk properties.
The hypothesis is falsified if processing time is not reduced by at least 50% relative to full-scale simulation methods.
